candidate: Local working tree based on 81f183a3; no deployment or push.
scope: Local backend, benchmark, tests and documentation. Backup work remains deferred.
changes: Group-scoped, lazy name/current-role catalog for collaborators in non-deleted member reports; roster selection, snapshots and source order preserved.

Request-owned collaborator-cost loader batches same-turn requests and reuses in-flight/fulfilled data for overlapping IDs across group members; failures reject all affected callers and evict failed IDs.
No cross-request cache, pool increase, production limiter or changed financial rules.
Benchmark can distribute existing RDOs between both group members without increasing report/service/person volume; cleanup removes moved reports first.
Benchmark-only databaseQueriesPeak measures submitted, unfinished pg.Pool.query calls per request, including pool waiting; report parser remains compatible with older traces.
httpMethod: Synthetic loopback HTTP against the real Express app and migrated PostgreSQL. Authentication validates persisted hashed sessions through requireAuth; password login is not exercised. First-process samples use a fresh API process per request, with warm database pages and process imports excluded. Warm requests mix surfaces, profiles and two sessions per profile under a bounded shared concurrency. Client timing includes response-body receipt; server timing includes authentication and serialization. Active-pool interval samples are observations, not individual query wait times. No Nginx, TLS, browser rendering, external API or production load is measured.

comparisonDesign.http: Two sequential equivalent synthetic cohorts, current harness for both sources, view=summary and distributed member RDOs. Not paired/randomized replicated latency trials.
comparisonDesign.postgres: PostgreSQL 16, one CPU, 768 MiB, disposable loopback-only container.
comparisonDesign.workloadComparability: The distributed fixture exercises both group members and additional fallback combinations. Its counts, payloads and timings must not be directly compared with earlier single-member-heavy fixtures.
comparisonDesign.sourceParity: Baseline and candidate in separate Node processes against exactly the same PostgreSQL rows; assert.deepEqual of complete outputs after Decimal/Map/Set JSON normalization; repeated after role-name, salary and report-hour writes.
comparisonDesign.sourceParityFixture: 120 RDOs distributed between two members plus three auxiliary reports and two added RDOs, planned role hours, day/night shifts, people without point, role history and role without cost profile.
comparisonDesign.queryPeakMeaning: Maximum submitted unfinished pool queries within one request, including queries queued in pg; not executing SQL count or connection count. Does not throttle or hide work.
comparisonDesign.refreshTimeOrigin: After worker writes acknowledged and sampling phase prepared; not exact database commit timestamp. Immediate card freshness not asserted.

covers: Overlapping/same-turn/in-flight requests share reads and preserve result fields.
Empty/missing IDs and separate request factories.
Failure propagation and retry without retained rejected cache.
Exact complete member/group parity and monetary values.
Single lazy identity catalog restricted to member reports; excludes private nonmember-only person.
One read for shared fallback collaborator across sequential member assembly.
Mismatched access/channel/admin-category scope and divisions cannot reuse scoped sources.
Updated name and manual cost-simulation exclusion visible in next group request.
Day/night role hours, point response projections and access contracts preserved.
Distributed member workload, submitted query peak, authentication/permissions, worker freshness and trace privacy.
Operational rows preserved when refusing nonempty benchmark database; visibly incomplete failure artifact.
Summary phase/status/p95 rules, bounded concurrency and old trace compatibility.
Current/history/full and progress-only, group/division, viewer permissions, shared commercial read and worker revision.

backendSuite.execution: Standalone full backend suite; live PostgreSQL opt-in suites run separately.

validation.syntax: Changed application and benchmark modules passed node --check.
validation.frontend: No frontend changes; suite/build/lint/budgets were validated in the d194dad8 stage and not repeated here.
validation.ci: Existing jobs already execute updated unit and PostgreSQL contracts; workflow unchanged.

limitations: Pool no-queue observations 24.9% before and 27.4% after; target 95% remains unmet. Peak waiting increased 36 to 42 and longest observed waiting sequence 311.1 to 316.9 ms.
Per-request query peaks remained: cards 3, individual detail 18, group 14, point 17. Lower total group queries did not lower its observed peak.
Pool interval observations depend on event-loop timing and are not individual query wait durations. No observed waiting run over five seconds.
Only one cold sample per route/profile; no cold p95 or general cold acceptance. No Nginx/TLS/browser/external API/production load measured.
Sequential p95 observations do not establish universal/causal speedup. Viewer individual detail p95 was about 2.6% slower in candidate cohort.
Point and individual financial calculation/query paths are unchanged; improvements observed there are not claimed as direct code gains.
Response sizes unchanged within each corresponding workload; different payload sizes vs previous evidence reflect the distributed fixture.
nextLocalWork: Investigate source overlap in individual detail and point (18/17 pending submitted queries per request). Compare total HTTP latency and explicitly measure any application-side wait before adopting coordination; do not merely move the pg pool queue.
